concept: Why do prices rise when a harvest fails?
title: Harvest Market
tagline: When fields fail, why do stalls charge more?

science.hiddenLaw: Law of supply and demand (competitive market clearing): price adjusts to equate quantity supplied and quantity demanded; a decrease in supply (leftward shift of the supply curve) with demand held constant raises the equilibrium price and lowers the equilibrium quantity traded.
science.plainStatement: When a harvest fails there is less to sell but the same number of buyers still want it, so buyers compete and bid the price up until the amount people are willing to buy shrinks to match the smaller amount available.
misconceptions: Prices rise because sellers become greedier or collude to gouge buyers, not because of scarcity - predicts price would rise even without a supply-demand imbalance and would not fall when supply recovers.
Price is set only by the cost of production - predicts that if growing costs haven't changed, price should stay the same after a harvest failure despite scarcity.

When supply falls, the same total amount is still sold and price rises just enough to keep farmers' total revenue constant - predicts quantity traded stays unchanged, ignoring that higher prices reduce quantity demanded.

story.mystery: Why does a smaller harvest make bread cost more?
story.goal: Adjust harvest and crowds to see how price finds balance.

transfer.setup: A city reservoir drops to half after drought, but same households still need water.
transfer.question: In a competitive market, what happens to water price and amount sold?
options: Price stays same, same amount sold

checks.description: Halving harvest supply with demand constant must raise market price above baseline
Control: with supply and demand both at baseline, price stays near baseline - removing scarcity removes price rise
Halving supply must lower equilibrium quantity traded, not keep it constant
If demand falls together with supply, price does not rise - price rise requires imbalance, not supply alone or greed
